issues.legal_issue: Separate first information reports and investigations may proceed for the same incident when they present different versions of events.
material_facts: Two reports concerned the same dacoity and killing but gave materially different accounts of who committed the offences.
The complainant in one report was himself facing trial in connection with the incident described in the other report.
issues.conclusion: The complainant’s pending trial and the fact that both reports concerned the same incident did not bar proceedings based on the other report, because the reports presented different versions.
issues.legal_principle: The sameness test applies to multiple reports concerning one incident; separate reports are permissible where they set out different versions, allowing cross-cases or counter-cases. The Court relied on Ram Lal Narang v. State (Delhi Admn.), Sudhir v. State of M.P., T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala, Upkar Singh v. Ved Prakash, and Babubhai v. State of Gujarat.

predicates.multiple_report_proceeding: The matter concerns multiple reports and investigations arising from one incident.
predicates.same_incident: The reports concern the same incident.
predicates.different_versions: The reports give materially different accounts of the events or the persons responsible.

issues.definition: When multiple reports concern the same incident but give different versions, separate reports and investigations are permissible.

issues.legal_issue: A second protest petition treated as a complaint may be entertained in exceptional circumstances when the earlier petition was not decided on its merits and the later petition supplies the material needed for consideration.
material_facts: The first protest petition was filed before the police submitted its final report, was not pursued, and was not acted on by the court.
After the final report was filed, a second protest petition was submitted with further particulars.
The Magistrate considered depositions from the complainant and numerous witnesses and examined the record of the related trial before finding a prima facie case and issuing summons.
The High Court quashed the Magistrate’s order on the ground that the second protest petition was not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The second protest petition was maintainable in the circumstances, and the High Court’s order was set aside and the Magistrate’s order restored.
issues.legal_principle: A protest petition may be treated as a complaint and proceeded with under Chapter XV of the Code of Criminal Procedure. There is no statutory bar to a second complaint on the same facts in exceptional circumstances, including where the earlier matter was decided on insufficient material, without understanding the complaint, on an incomplete record, or where relevant facts were not previously available; a second complaint is not maintainable after a full merits consideration. The Court relied on sections 203 and 204 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Bhagwant Singh v. Commissioner of Police, Bindeshwari Prasad Singh v. Kali Singh, Pramatha Nath Talukdar v. Saroj Ranjan Sarkar, Mahesh Chand v. B. Janardhan Reddy, Poonam Chand Jain v. Fazru, Jatinder Singh v. Ranjit Kaur, and Ranvir Singh v. State of Haryana.

rule.if: second_complaint_proceeding and second_protest_petition_filed and earlier_petition_not_decided_on_merits and later_petition_supplied_material_for_consideration

predicates.second_complaint_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a later complaint or protest petition following an earlier one about the same matter.
predicates.second_protest_petition_filed: The complainant filed a later protest petition after the earlier petition.
predicates.earlier_petition_not_decided_on_merits: The court did not dispose of the earlier petition after fully considering the complainant’s case on its merits.
predicates.later_petition_supplied_material_for_con: The later petition supplied particulars or other material needed for the court to consider whether proceedings should continue.

issues.definition: A later protest petition may be entertained when the earlier petition was not decided on its merits and the later petition supplies material needed for consideration.
